prerequisites: Mathematics knowledge in real functions, differential and integral calculus, as taught in Mathematics 1 and 2 modules of Electrical Engineering or Computer Science degree programs.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know and possess a good understanding of the basic concepts, facts and reasoning methods of probability theory and statistics.
Students can model events of medium complexity and calculate associated probabilities.
They can handle common statistical procedures and evaluate their results. In particular, they can assess which statistical method is appropriate for a given problem.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Probability Theory: Concepts of event and probability, conditional probability, total probability, independence, random variables, law of large numbers, standard distributions.
Introduction to the basic methods of descriptive and inferential statistics: common estimation and testing procedures
Linear models: Variance and covariance analysis, stochastic treatment of linear regression
Supplementary: Introduction to a statistics package (e.g., R)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either a project report (written) or an exam. The duration of the exam is according to the applicable study regulations. A written project report should be 5-10 pages, with an associated explanation of approximately 15 minutes.
